title: Maine Barn Weddings | R&SVP – Hio Ridge, Bridgton
description: Sunday weddings for up to 135 guests in a restored 1820 barn in Bridgton, Maine. Ceremony in the field, reception in the barn. Alcohol-free. May through October.
heading: Weddings
lede: The mountain in front of you and everyone you love behind you. Then dinner under beams raised in 1820, on a farm one family has kept since 1941.
hero_alt: Ceremony benches in the field at Hio Ridge, birches and the tree line behind

day.heading: The day, the way it goes here

steps.title: Morning in the ell
steps.body: Your dress on its hook, your people on the benches, the field outside the window. The groom's room is across the hall.

steps.title: Vows in the field
steps.body: Benches made from the barn's old floorboards, facing Pleasant Mountain. If it rains, you marry under the beams and lose nothing.

steps.title: Dinner under the beams
steps.body: Long tables down the barn or rounds with room to dance. Your caterer works in the prep kitchen. The French doors stay open to the patio.

steps.title: The string lights come on
steps.body: The field goes gold, the patio fills, and the last photographs are the ones you keep.

sunday.heading: Why a Sunday
sunday.body: Saturday is our day of rest, so our weddings are on Sundays. Most couples find the photographer and the band they want are open, the weekend starts a day early for guests who travel, and the day itself is quieter. [CONFIRM: wording Susan is comfortable with]

faq.q: How many guests can the barn hold?
faq.a: 135. That is the capacity on our town permit for any event.

faq.q: Can we have our ceremony outside?
faq.a: Yes. The ceremony field faces Pleasant Mountain, with benches made from the barn's old floorboards. In rain, the ceremony moves into the barn.
You marry in the barn, under the beams, with the French doors open. The ceremony rows are set either way, so nothing is decided until the morning.

faq.q: Can we bring our own caterer?
faq.a: Yes. There is a prep kitchen with barn doors your caterer can close while they finish the meal.
No. We are an alcohol-free venue, and that is part of our town permit. Many couples tell us it makes for a family day.
Yes. We are a family venue. Grandparents, babies and the flower girl's little brother are all welcome.
No. Our weddings are on Sundays, and we also book weekdays.
May through October. October is our favorite.
Yes. 6-foot and 8-foot tables, 5-foot rounds, and chairs for the ceremony and the reception.
Yes. There are three accessible parking spaces in the driveway, a wooden ramp to the main floor, an ADA accessible bathroom, and a paved path around the barn to the patio.
Email or text Susan to schedule a tour. After the tour we send the contract and the pricing brochure. [CONFIRM: deposit and booking steps]

faq.q: How long do we have the barn?
faq.a: The whole day. [CONFIRM: access window, setup the day before, end time]
The same day, by email or text, most days. [CONFIRM: Susan's reply time]

closing.heading: Pick your Sunday
closing.body: No date yet? Most couples don't have one when they start looking. Tell us the season and about how many guests, and we will send the open Sundays and the pricing brochure.
